newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish eviction siege ends peacefully.
newsitem.headline: Irish eviction siege ends peacefully.

text.p: A German who barricaded himself into an Irish cottage for three days to protest against his eviction left the house peacefully on Friday, police said.

Gerrit Isenborges, 41, from Duesseldorf, shot and wounded three council officers who tried to serve him an eviction notice before barricading himself into the cottage near Ballyconnell in County Cavan on Wednesday.
None of the three council officers was seriously injured.
Police also confirmed that Isenborges' 82-year old mother, who was in the cottage with him, had died. She was terminally ill with cancer.

Isenborges has lived in the area for about three years after working as a caretaker at a nearby "Wild West" theme park. His eviction is sought by the cottage's owner, Austrian Michael Hehle, who also owns the theme park.
Hehle told Irish media that Isenborges failed to carry out agreed repairs to the house or pay any bills.
